title: Fourteen Autumns and One Short Map
subtitle: 行星探索 · 主题语境阅读
theme: 行星探索（宇宙探索·行星与地球）
meta: 主题语境：行星探索（宇宙探索·行星与地球）　|　核心词汇：earth　|　正文 346 words　|　高三一轮复习
intro: 请阅读文章，根据上下文判断每一处 earth 的含义，再完成 Task 1—Task 3。
passage: In 1969 my teacher ① measured the earth that no student in the room would have believed, and he said the measuring was the whole of the autumn. The ② earth, meaning the planet and not the soil, turned fourteen autumns and stayed unnamed in the book; the earth, he said, is the only thing in a room that is judged by how long it is left unmeasured.

Every ③ earth in that room had the same short map at the end of it, and the ④ earth at the end, meaning the one they kept for the next class and not either of those, was the only one anybody ever thanked twice. An earth, my mother said, is nine parts patience and one part somebody willing to measure; my teacher said the measuring is the part that fills fourteen autumns.

My uncle meant the other thing entirely: he said ⑤ the earth was the whole of the story, meaning the soil and not the planet. The ⑥ earth, meaning the soil and not any of that, is the only thing in a story that everybody treads on and nobody notices; earth, he said, is either something you measure or the only word that means both a planet and a soil. He said the soil is the part they remember.

By 1978 the ⑦ earth had become a line in a star chart, and the star chart had become an argument about the short map. The ⑧ earth of the whole thing, my teacher wrote in October, was one room and fourteen autumns of measuring; earth, he said, is either the one at the end or the reason you learned to measure. She said the measuring was never mentioned.

The ⑨ earth I remember is the one named in the star chart, which rose in 1990 and is still described as the quietest in the room. An ⑩ earth, my mother said in 1992, is the only one that improves by being measured; every earth, she said, is a soil that has agreed to look like a planet. She said the soil was the honest half.

task1.title: Task 1　语境辨义
task1.intro: 请将对应义项填入表中。
options: A. n. 地球（指那间教室里讲到的那一颗）
B. n. 地球（指那颗行星本身，与泥土相对）
C. 固定搭配：measure the earth 测量地球
D. n. 地球（指留给下一班观测的那一颗）
E. n. 地球（抽象总称，指一间教室的观星之事）
F. n. 地球（指星图上写到、被标名的那一颗）
G. n. 泥土；土壤（指故事里人人都踩却无人留意的那样东西）
H. n. 泥土；土壤（抽象总称，指人人都踩却无人留意的那种东西）

answers.why: measure the earth 意为“测量地球”，1969 年老师测了一间教室里没有一个学生肯相信的地球。
earth 意为“地球”，指那颗行星本身而不是泥土，它转了十四个秋天而在簿子上没有名字。
earth 意为“地球”，指那间教室里讲到的每一颗地球，每一颗后头都有同一张小小的地图。
earth 意为“地球”，指留给下一班观测的那一颗，是唯一有人谢过两次的。
earth 意为“泥土、土壤”，指故事里人人都踩却无人留意的那样东西，叔叔说这泥土就是那个故事的全部。
earth 意为“泥土、土壤”，指人人都踩却无人留意的那种东西而不是那颗行星，是故事里人人都踩、却无人留意的东西。
earth 意为“地球”，指星图上写到、被标名的那一颗，到 1978 年这颗地球成了星图里的一行。
earth 意为“地球”，老师十月写道，整件事的观星之事是一间教室和十四个秋天的测量。
earth 意为“地球”，我记得的是星图上标名的那一颗，1990 年升起来了，至今仍被说成教室里最安静的一颗。
earth 为抽象总称，母亲 1992 年说，一颗地球是唯一会因为被好好测量而变得更好的东西。
